correctness.rationale: Exact two-branch identity x′+y′−x−y=μ+α|x|−g(y) follows since the branch linear x coefficient cancels δ. For ε=min(1/8,α/(8(1+D))) and η≤r/(2(1+D)), both |g(y)|≤ε|y| and |g(y′)|≤ε(D|x|+|g(y)|) hold at all pre-exit points. With Φ=x+y−g(y)−|g(y)|, ΔΦ≥μ+(α−2εD)|x|+(1−2ε)|g(y)|≥μ. Φ is bounded by 9η/4 in Bη, so its range <5η; at N=floor(5η/μ)+1 consecutive internal steps the monotone gain would exceed that range. Handles x=0 continuity, arbitrary δ signs, arbitrary μ, and g not differentiable; only local first departure is proved.
